oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Growth performance and biomass production of Eleusine indica and Rorippa sylvestris on heavy metal contaminated soil after biochar application
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Priyadarshini, Rossyda
Hamzah, Amir
Astuti, Astuti
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: S Agriculture (General)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Heavy metal contamination was an environmental and human health problem all over the world. Cadmium is the most hazardous heavy metals due to its high mobility and toxicity at low concentrations. Lead (Pb) also belongs to the hazard element caused by its prolonged persistence in the soil. This study aimed to develop the remediation techniques on polluted land, i.e. a combination of biochar and indigenous plant. The biochar was produced by slow pyrolysis method. This experiment was conducted at the farmland at Sumber Brantas, Malang, East Java. We used rice husk and tobacco waste biochar, and Eleusine indica (L.) Gaertn and Rorippa sylvestris (L.) Bess. as remediator plants. The results showed that rice husk biochar had a significant effect on pH value and potassium content (p = 0.0001; p=0.0004). On the contrary, the soil nitrogen content, soil organic-C content, and soil cation exchange capacity applied with tobacco waste biochar application were higher than that applied with rice husk biochar (p = 0.03; p=0.00001; p = 0.00001). The improvement of soil characteristics increased the growth of Eleusine indica and Rorippa sylvestris as indicated by the plant height and biomass. The addition of biochar could promote the growth of remediator plant and enhanced the accumulation of Pb and Cd in the plants. Mixtures of rice husk biochar and tobacco waste biochar caused Eleusine indica more effectively absorbed heavy metals than Rorippa sylvestris on all types of biochar treatments; Eleusine indica absorbed Pb and Cd higher than Rorippa sylvestris as shown by Pb and Cd contents in the soil. Keywords: biochar, heavy metal contaminated soil, phytoremediation
oai_dc:dc.dc:identifier: Priyadarshini, Rossyda and Hamzah, Amir and Astuti, Astuti (2020) Growth performance and biomass production of Eleusine indica and Rorippa sylvestris on heavy metal contaminated soil after biochar application. Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management, 7 (4). ISSN 2339-076X

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: EKSPLORASI POTENSI PRODUK UNGGULAN PERTANIAN DAN KETERPADUANNYA MENDUKUNG DESA WISATA TAMANSARI (DEWI TARI)
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Priyadarshini, Rossyda
Maroeto, Maroeto
Santoso, Wahyu
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: S Agriculture (General)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The tourism village is a place that has certain characteristics and values that can be a special attraction for tourists with a special interest in rural life. This paper aims to identify people's perceptions of the potential of superior agricultural products to support the development of Tamansari Tourism Village (DEWI TARI) in Tamansari Village, Licin District, Banyuwangi Regency. The method of presenting data is done with a qualitative descriptive approach and chi square. Leading sector of Tamansari village is in agriculture, plantation and livestock sector of superior commodities in the form of coffee, rice, cattle, goats and cloves. The leading forestry, wood products and non-timber commodities are in the form of sengon and mahoni. Main commodities of fisheries are tilapia, koi fish and carp. Indicators of village superior products have a strong correlation with various agricultural sectors and are well perceived by the community

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Metagenomic Sequencing Analysis and Microbial Identification on Various Landcover
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Priyadarshini, Rossyda
Syafriani, Elly
Somala, Medina Uli Alba
Hamzah, Amir
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: S Agriculture (General)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Soil degradation will affect the availability of soil nutrients. Microbes role was important in supplying soil nutrient. How is microbes supply the nutrients can be learned through the metagenome technique. Metagenome is one of the molecular techniques that can identify microbial communities from soil samples that are used quickly and precisely. Through the metagenome technique, not only information about the identity of microbial species can be obtained, but also the enzymes produced, which will affect the soil nutrients availability. This study aims to detect and identify the impact of land cover types on microbial types. Soil samples were taken under agricultural land (LP) and agroforestry (AF). Each type of land cover was taken at 4 (four) different locations. The method used in this research is a molecular-based species identification method through metagenome analysis. This study showed that there are variations in microbial species in various types of land cover. This information is important for sustainable agricultural management in the future. Our study showed that on all of the land cover types, Proteobacteria were the most abundant phylum in all of the land cover patterns. Among them, s_Sphingomonas_melonis; f_Sphingomonadaceae; g_Sphingomonas; c_Alphaproteobacteria; p_Proteobacteria; and o_Sphingomonadales were the most abundant in the LP groups, while p_Acidobacteria and c_Deltaproteobacteria were the most abundant in AF groups. This composition of soil metagenomic was associated with the soil physic-chemical properties, especially pH and soil organic matter. Keywords: metagenomic technique, soil bacteria, 16S rRNA gene amplicon, land cover types
oai_dc:dc.dc:identifier: Priyadarshini, Rossyda and Syafriani, Elly and Somala, Medina Uli Alba and Hamzah, Amir (2019) Metagenomic Sequencing Analysis and Microbial Identification on Various Landcover. In: 4th Internasional Research Month.

Baon, John Bako
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: S Agriculture (General)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Shade -grown coffee is an agricultural system that cointans some forest-like characteristics. However structure and diversity are poorly known in shade coffee systems. In 8 coffee-grown plots of Ngantang-Malang structural variables of shade vegetation and coffee yields were measured recording spesies and their use. Coffee stands had four strata with mean density 3381 trees per hectare and at least there were three spesies on each plot. Diametric distribution resembles of a secondary forest. There is a significant role of shade-grown coffee as diversity refuge for woody plants and maybe associated fauna.Key words: Diversity, shade-grown coffee , vegetation structure, woody plants, agroecosystems.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: ANALISIS PEMBENTUKAN ASIAN INFRASTRUCTURE INVESTMENT BANK (AIIB) OLEH CINA PADA TAHUN 2016
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Sihite, Evelyn Saraswati
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: JZ International relations
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a multilateral development bank with mission and aim to improve social welfare and economic growth in the Asian region through the investment flow and infrastructure development. The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) was officially operational in 2016 based on initiative of President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperations (APEC) Leaders forum on October 2013 in Bali, Indonesia. The initiation of this financial institution establishment is actually China response to the condition of infrastructure gap in the Asian region. That many countries in this region, particularly developing countries do not have sufficient financial capacities to build infrastructure facilities. In consequence, there is an infrastructure gap in this region so that regional welfare has not been maximally reached. This research is specifically intended to analyze China action in the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) establishment in 2016. The analysis will be conducted by the theory of great power diplomacy and the concept of national attributes. That China as a great power in the Asian region has the responsibility to ensure regional welfare and stability. And this is manifested by establishing the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) as an instrument to raise up welfare and stability in the Asian region. In addition, the national attributes owned by China in the form of size and territory (as the largest country in the Asian region) and economic capabilities (as the largest economy in the Asian region) also espouse the existence of China in establishing the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) in the Asian region. The research scope is from 2010, when China began to influence as a great power in the Asian region until 2016, when the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) began operating officially and undertaking several infrastructure projects in the Asian region. Keywords: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), China, great power diplomacy, size and territory, economic capabilities, Asian region, welfare and stability.
